TOORO KINGDOM: QUEEN MOTHER HIGHLIGHTS LEGACY PROJECTS IN MEMORY OF LATE KING OYO.

By Keefa Nuwahereza.

The graphic depicting a ceremonial moment involving the Tooro Kingdom’s Queen Mother Best Kemigisa alongside text outlining developments announced in memory of the late Omukama Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV. The image and accompanying details form part of a broader public effort by the late king’s immediate family to preserve and extend his influence through concrete institutions and programmes. These initiatives emerge against a backdrop of personal loss, cultural continuity, and ongoing internal tensions within the kingdom following a reign that began in childhood and ended prematurely.

King Oyo was born on 16 April 1992 as the son of Omukama Patrick David Matthew Kaboyo Rwamuhokya Olimi III and Queen Mother Best Kemigisa. His father died suddenly on 26 August 1995. Traditional rites installed the three-year-old prince as Omukama on 12 September 1995, making him the world’s youngest reigning monarch at the time, a distinction noted in contemporary records. He held the full title Rukirabasaija Omukama Oyo Nyimba Kabamba-Iguru Rukidi IV. Because of his age, regents and senior royal figures managed cultural affairs during his minority. He assumed fuller personal responsibility around his 18th birthday in 2010. He pursued education in Uganda and later obtained a bachelor’s degree in Business Management from the University of Winchester in the United Kingdom in 2013. Throughout his roughly 31-year reign he emphasised cultural preservation alongside practical development in agriculture, youth skills, health, sport, and environmental matters. He served as a UNAIDS goodwill ambassador and supported campaigns against HIV/AIDS. He established or advanced initiatives such as the King Oyo Model Farm at Bugaaki in Kyenjojo District for demonstration of commercial farming, agricultural education centres distributing seedlings, and partnerships on immunisation and youth employment. In 2025 he offered approximately 50 acres of private land to the government for a stadium in the Fort Portal area. He died on 27 August 2026 at the age of 34 in the United States after treatment for angiosarcoma, a rare and aggressive cancer. He was buried at the Karambi Royal Tombs on 12 September 2026. President Yoweri Museveni directed an official burial and ordered flags at half-mast.

Queen Mother Best Kemigisa, born on 22 April 1967, became queen consort through marriage to Olimi III and later Queen Mother upon her son’s accession. She participated in regency arrangements during his childhood and lost a young daughter, Princess Cecilia Komukyeya, to leukaemia in 1997. Her only surviving child is Princess Ruth Nsemere Komuntale. After King Oyo’s death she and her daughter issued statements of appreciation for public and presidential support during the illness, repatriation, and funeral. They outlined a commitment to convert mourning into practical legacy work rather than solely ceremonial remembrance. President Museveni agreed to serve as patron and founding chairman of the proposed King Oyo Memorial Foundation, providing a framework for the family’s stated goals.

The graphic lists five interconnected developments under the memorial effort. The King Oyo Memorial Foundation is intended as the coordinating body. It would preserve personal belongings, documents, and objects from the late king’s life for educational and cultural purposes while supporting community projects. The King Oyo Tooro Museum is planned to house a permanent collection of those items, document the progression from child monarch to adult ruler, and present the wider history and culture of Tooro, including its 19th-century origins when a prince from Bunyoro established a separate realm near the Rwenzori Mountains. Proponents expect the museum to contribute to tourism in Fort Portal. The King Oyo International Stadium revives a project linked to the 50-acre land donation made during the king’s lifetime. The family has expressed the wish that the facility be completed to provide a venue for talent development, school competitions, major events, and related careers in sport. The King Oyo Research and Teaching Hospital is proposed with dedicated centres for cancer and HIV research and treatment. It draws motivation from the late king’s own illness and is envisioned to include clinical care, training of health professionals, early-detection programmes, and research relevant to regional health burdens. The King Oyo Model Farm would expand the existing Bugaaki farm into a centre for agricultural education, innovation, value addition, and outreach to schools, youth, and farmers, building on earlier work promoting coffee, cocoa, livestock, and related enterprises.

These proposals align with themes visible during the reign: youth empowerment, practical skills, health access, sport as a developmental tool, and cultural continuity. The Queen Mother has described them as “his legacy put to work for the people” rather than monuments alone. As of early November 2026, the foundation itself remained at the planning and organisational stage, with no official launch date publicly confirmed by the immediate family. Princess Komuntale and the Queen Mother have publicly asserted that management rests exclusively with the immediate family and designated board members, warning against unauthorised claims or activities by extended relatives.

The memorial announcements occur within a contested succession environment. King Oyo’s 2022 will named a lawfully recognised biological son as primary heir to the Tooro throne, with fallback provisions naming other princes (including a son of the then Omusuuga) if the son were unable to succeed. The identity of that son has not been publicly disclosed; reports indicate he remained in the United States during the immediate post-death period. A 21-member committee of the Babiito royal clan selected Prince Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma (later styled Edward Rukidi Nyabongo I), a cousin and former journalist, as successor. He was publicly identified in early September 2026, performed traditional rites at the burial, and was crowned in late September 2026. Immediate family members, including the Queen Mother, contested the process, arguing that the will had not been fully respected and that burial should precede further succession debate. The Attorney General advised that the will should guide the matter. Disputes extended to control of the memorial foundation, with the immediate family rejecting involvement by certain cousins. Separate statements from clan leadership pledged continued support for the Queen Mother irrespective of the succession disagreement. The new Omukama has separately spoken about mobilising resources for cancer-related facilities in the late king’s memory.

Tooro Kingdom itself traces its modern form to the early 19th century and was restored as a cultural institution after the 1993 repeal of earlier abolition measures. Its Omukama holds primarily cultural authority under Uganda’s constitutional framework for traditional leaders. The late king’s tenure therefore combined symbolic continuity with concrete local initiatives in a setting where political power resides with the central government. The graphic shared on X in November 2026 captures one family’s public presentation of unfinished or expandable elements of that tenure—museum preservation of personal and historical material, completion of a stadium on donated land, expansion of an existing farm into a teaching facility, and a hospital oriented toward the diseases that affected the king and remain prevalent regionally.

The projects remain aspirational pending funding, land and planning clearances, institutional agreements, and resolution of any overlapping claims. Their stated purpose is to translate the late king’s interests in youth, agriculture, sport, health, and cultural identity into durable local assets. The X post itself functions as a concise visual summary of that intention, circulating the list of developments at a moment when both the foundation’s control and the broader succession question continued to generate public statements from different branches of the royal family. Further official updates from the foundation’s recognised organisers or from kingdom structures will determine the pace and form of implementation.

Kimi K3.1 Pro is FREE on NVIDIA right now, and you can try it without an API key. 😳

Moonshot AI's powerful model is now available through NVIDIA's playground.
Here's how to access it:
Go to https://t.co/yJvUxjjpTz

Sign in or create an NVIDIA account.

Open Models and search for Kimi K3.1 Pro.

Select the model with the Free Endpoint tag.

Open the Playground and start chatting.

Why it's worth testing:
→ 1 million token context window
→ 2.8T total parameters, 104B activated
→ Agentic coding and complex reasoning
→ 3D modeling and financial research
→ Text and image understanding

Important: The free endpoint is currently available for playground use only. 

NVIDIA explicitly says programmatic API access is not available yet, and generating an API key won't unlock it.
